# Design: issue-292-spike-cloudflare-private-origins-as-mctl

## Current state

`mctlhq/.github` holds roadmap manifests and spike reports. It holds no runtime
code. A spike delivers three things:

- a report in `docs/spikes/<name>.md`, for example `docs/spikes/edge-config-kv-instant.md` and `docs/spikes/mcp-gateway-g0.md`;
- a `SpikeDefinition` in `roadmap/spikes/<name>.yaml`, for example `roadmap/spikes/edge-config-kv-instant.yaml`, which records `lifecycle: proposed`, the issue, the allowed `outcomes` and `evidence.report`;
- a link under "Spikes" in `AGENTS.md`.

The schema is `roadmap/schemas/spike-definition.schema.json`. Outcomes must match
`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$` and at least two are required. Validation runs through
`roadmap/scripts/validate.py` (README: `python roadmap/scripts/validate.py
roadmap/epics roadmap/spikes`), with tests in `roadmap/tests/test_validate_spike.py`
and CI in `.github/workflows/roadmap-validate.yml`. The convention, visible in
`edge-config-kv-instant.yaml`, is that the agent writes a *proposed* verdict in
the report only, and the owner records the decision. Spike issue bindings must
be unique among spikes. `mctlhq/.github#292` is not bound anywhere: the
`number: 292` in `roadmap/epics/devloop-pr-adoption.yaml` is
`mctlhq/mctl-agents#292`, a different repository.

How MCTL reaches things across network boundaries today. All in mctl-gitops,
read at commit `5480dce379d030ea55f175600f9417211a33f34a`.

- **One plain Cloudflare Tunnel already exists.**
  - `infrastructure/cloudflare/account/events-tunnel.tf` declares `cloudflare_zero_trust_tunnel_cloudflared.platform_events` (`config_src = "cloudflare"`).
  - Its ingress config routes hostname `events-valkey.mctl.ai` to `tcp://valkey.platform-events.svc.cluster.local:6379`, with a required `http_status:404` catch-all.
  - A `non_identity` Access policy admits a single hand-created service token. The `self_hosted` Access application has `allowed_idps = []`.
  - The connector is `platform-gitops/infra-components/data/valkey/cloudflared.yaml`: an outbound-only `cloudflare/cloudflared:2026.10.5` Deployment. Its token comes from Vault `secret/platform/events-tunnel` and is mounted as a file. It runs non-root with a read-only filesystem.
  - `infra-components/data/valkey/networkpolicy.yaml` admits the connector pod.
  - Secrets stay out of OpenTofu state: the tunnel secret is generated by Cloudflare and the service token is referenced only by id.
  - This is the "public hostname, private origin, no inbound port" pattern the issue describes, in MCTL's own account, without Private Origins.
- **The stale comment.** `platform-gitops/argocd/templates/networkpolicy.yaml`, dated 2026-10-12, still says "There is no cloudflared tunnel in the cluster". It predates the events tunnel. This only matters as a doc inconsistency to note.
- **MCP upstreams are public origins behind the Cloudflare MCP Portal.**
  - `infrastructure/cloudflare/portal/mcp-servers.tf` registers `tg`, `projects`, `alice`, `coolify`, `seerrsense` and `api` with public hostnames (`https://coolify.mctl.ai/mcp`, ...).
  - `portal/README.md` documents that per-user OAuth grants and runtime sync status are deliberately not in Git.
  - `account/projects-mcp.tf` shows the other Access pattern: Access is the OAuth authorization server, and the origin verifies `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion`.
- **Planned MCP gateway.** `docs/plans/mcp-gateway.md` (epic `roadmap/epics/mcp-gateway.yaml`, `lifecycle: proposed`) will be the per-principal, per-tenant policy point in front of downstream MCP servers.
  - It calls downstreams as the user (RFC 8693 token exchange, "class A").
  - Its fail-closed table: policy unreachable means a retriable error, never "allow all".
  - `docs/spikes/mcp-gateway-g0.md` returned `REVISE`.
  - A tenant-private downstream would be one more entry in that gateway's downstream set.
- **Tenant egress.** `platform-gitops/tenants/*/values.yaml` sets `allowInternetEgress`. It is `true` for admins, erpact, labs and namax66, and `false` for commerce-proof, karabu and mctl. A caller reaching a Cloudflare hostname needs internet egress.
- **Cloudflare IaC is the established control plane.** The `cloudflare-iac` epic is `lifecycle: completed`. Changes go through `cloudflare-plan.yml`, `cloudflare-apply.yml` and nightly `cloudflare-drift.yml`, so any POC resource would be reviewed OpenTofu.
- **There is no MCTL-owned VPN or overlay.** No WireGuard, Tailscale or IPsec component appears under `platform-gitops/infra-components/`. MCTL owns no network overlay today, so "avoid building one" is a decision about the future, not a migration.

External fact `[DOC]`, from https://blog.cloudflare.com/private-origins-public-to-private/, fetched 2026-11-01:

- Private Origins lets a proxied A or AAAA record point at a private IP. It is generally available behind an entitlement enabled by the account team. Pricing and plan tier are not stated.
- It needs Cloudflare One connectivity. Unified Routing is required unless the connection is Cloudflare Tunnel.
- Supported connectivity: IPsec, GRE, CNI, Tunnel and Mesh. WAN and Mesh need a return route for `100.64.0.0/12` and `2606:4700:cf1:5000::/64`.
- The DNS record carries a `private_routing` attribute. It is forced on for RFC 1918, 6598 and 4193 addresses.
- Limits: no Argo Smart Routing, no dedicated egress IPs, and health checks need Load Balancing.
- Private-to-private, which explicitly includes AI agents on private networks, is targeted for a closed beta in early 2027.

Deployed state checked:

- `mctl_get_service_status(labs, coolify-mcp)`: Healthy and Synced, image `3.8.3`, host `coolify.mctl.ai`, port 8080, `base-service`. This is the candidate POC endpoint.
- `mctl_list_tenants`: refused ("requires admin access"). The tenant list was taken from the gitops directory `platform-gitops/tenants/` instead: admins, commerce-proof, erpact, karabu, labs, mctl, namax66. Whether any tenant runs a private-network tool could not be observed.
- `platform-gitops/services/labs/coolify-mcp/values.yaml`: `MCP_TENANCY: multi`, public ingress `coolify.mctl.ai` and `labs-coolify-mcp.mctl.ai` via cert-manager.
- `platform-gitops/infra-components/data/valkey/cloudflared.yaml` and `.../networkpolicy.yaml`: the events tunnel connector is declared, as described above. Its live pod status was not queried, because it is not a tenant service.
- Whether the MCTL Cloudflare account has the Private Origins entitlement, Cloudflare One WAN or Unified Routing: **could not be observed**. No OpenTofu resource references them, but absence from IaC is not proof of absence in the account. This is recorded under Open questions in requirements.md.

## Proposed solution

Deliver the spike as documentation and a manifest in `mctlhq/.github`, following
the existing spike convention. Change no infrastructure.

1. `docs/spikes/cloudflare-private-origins.md`. Structure:
   - Non-claims and evidence-tag legend, copied from the style of `edge-config-kv-instant.md`.
   - Evidence pins table (`.github`, `mctl-gitops` 40-hex SHAs, Cloudflare doc URLs with fetch dates).
   - Sections 1 to 10, one per investigation point in the issue.
   - A responsibility table, an alternatives matrix, a fail-closed matrix, the POC design, cost, the proposed verdict, a follow-up issue table, re-open triggers and open questions.
2. `roadmap/spikes/cloudflare-private-origins.yaml`. A `SpikeDefinition`:
   - `metadata.owner: mctlhq/.github`;
   - `lifecycle: proposed`;
   - `github.issue: mctlhq/.github#292`;
   - `outcomes: [ADOPT, POC, COMPLEMENTARY, NO_GO]`;
   - `execution.devloop: true`;
   - `evidence.report: docs/spikes/cloudflare-private-origins.md`;
   - a header comment saying that the proposed verdict lives in the report only.
3. `AGENTS.md`: one "Spikes" bullet linking the report and stating the proposed verdict.

### Analytical content the report must carry, with the provisional reasoning

**Proposed verdict: `COMPLEMENTARY`, with a bounded Tunnel-first POC.** The
report confirms or overturns it. The reasoning, grounded in what was read:

- **Point 2: overlap.** For a tenant that can run a connector, Private Origins over Tunnel offers MCTL almost nothing beyond the plain Tunnel and Access pattern already proven in `events-tunnel.tf`. Both give a proxied hostname, a private origin, no inbound port and the same Access gate. Private Origins adds value in two cases:
  - (a) tenants already on Cloudflare WAN (IPsec, GRE or CNI), who need no connector software at all;
  - (b) origins addressed by private IP through Mesh, where one connector serves many origins.
  These are enterprise topologies, not the default tenant.
- **Point 3: a tenant-private MCP server is feasible.** Use a proxied hostname per tenant tool, for example `<tool>.<tenant>.<zone>`, whose origin is reachable only via tunnel or Private Origins. Put an Access application in front with a per-tenant service token (`non_identity`) for MCTL's caller. The MCP server additionally verifies an MCTL-issued audience-bound token, as in gateway class A, so Access alone never authorizes a tool call.
- **Point 4: onboarding and trust boundaries.** Two modes.
  - *MCTL-account mode.* MCTL's OpenTofu creates a tunnel per tenant, its ingress (one hostname, 404 catch-all), DNS and Access. The connector token goes to the tenant out of band. The tenant runs `cloudflared` next to the tool. Trust: the tenant trusts MCTL's Cloudflare account to route only MCTL traffic. MCTL holds connector-token issuance and revocation.
  - *Tenant-account mode.* The tenant creates the Private Origins or Tunnel hostname and the Access app in its own Cloudflare account, and issues MCTL a service token. MCTL holds only that token, in Vault under `teams/<tenant>/...`. MCTL owns no tenant network object.
  - The report recommends tenant-account mode for enterprise tenants with Cloudflare One, and MCTL-account Tunnel mode for everyone else.
- **Point 5: fail closed.** Every failure path ends in a failed call:
  - Access default-deny, plus the tunnel catch-all 404;
  - connector down gives a Cloudflare 1033 or 502;
  - a missing return route times out;
  - service token revoked or expired gives an Access 403;
  - the gateway's policy endpoint down gives a retriable error, per the `mcp-gateway.md` fail-closed table;
  - tenant origin down gives a 502 and an error.
  The one thing that is not fail-closed by construction is an Access application accidentally deleted while its DNS record stays. The report must show that the tunnel's origin still demands the MCTL token (defence in depth), and that nightly `cloudflare-drift.yml` detects the deletion.
- **Point 6: isolation and identity.**
  - Isolation unit: one tunnel, one hostname, one Access app and one service token per tenant. There is no shared connector across tenants, and no Mesh shared across tenants.
  - Identity propagation: Access sees only MCTL's service token. The end-user principal travels in the MCTL-issued token, so Cloudflare never carries authority.
  - Audit correlation: log `Cf-Ray` together with the gateway's `gateway_request_id` and `downstream_audit_id`.
  - Revocation has three independent levers: revoke the service token (Cloudflare), delete the tunnel or rotate the connector token, or revoke the MCTL grant (mctl-api).
- **Point 7: alternatives.** See below. An MCTL-owned overlay is rejected on operational cost.
- **Point 8: what MCTL still owns.** See the responsibility table below.
- **Point 9: private-to-private.** It would remove the need for a public hostname at all: an MCTL caller on a Cloudflare-connected private network would reach the tenant network directly. That would shrink MCTL's DNS and Access surface. It is pre-beta (early 2027), so it is a re-open trigger, not an input to the decision.
- **Point 10: POC.** See below.

**Responsibility table (core of the decision):**

| Responsibility | Owner after integration | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Encrypted transport to a network with no public ingress | Cloudflare (Tunnel / WAN / Mesh) | tenant connector or WAN |
| TLS termination, WAF, rate limit, DDoS at the edge | Cloudflare | zone config via OpenTofu |
| Network admission (is this caller MCTL?) | Cloudflare Access (service token) | `account/*.tf` |
| Per-tenant tunnel, DNS, Access objects as code, drift detection | MCTL | mctl-gitops `infrastructure/cloudflare/` |
| Connector token and service token custody, rotation, revocation | MCTL | Vault + runbook |
| Tenant onboarding and offboarding workflow | MCTL | mctl-api operation (future) |
| Principal identity, delegated authority, per-tool policy | MCTL | mctl-api + MCP gateway |
| Approvals, budgets, audit, correlation | MCTL | mctl-api, gateway audit |
| Tenant-to-endpoint registry (which tenant tool lives at which hostname) | MCTL | gateway downstream config |
| Health of tenant connectivity surfaced to the user | MCTL (reads Cloudflare status) | monitoring |

MCTL avoids: running VPN servers or peers, an IP address plan, NAT and
routing, key exchange, and a connector fleet inside tenant networks.

**POC design, which the report fixes in detail:**

- Target: the existing `labs/coolify-mcp`, as a stand-in for a tenant-private origin.
- A new OpenTofu tunnel `mctl-poc-private-mcp`, `config_src = "cloudflare"`, with ingress hostname `coolify-private.mctl.ai` pointing to `http://coolify-mcp.labs.svc.cluster.local:8080` and a 404 catch-all.
- A connector Deployment cloned from `cloudflared.yaml`, in `labs`.
- A `self_hosted` Access application with `allowed_idps = []` and a `non_identity` service-token policy, as in `events-tunnel.tf`.
- Caller: a one-shot Argo or `curl` job that sends MCP `initialize` and `tools/list` with the service token plus a user token. Later, the MCP gateway.
- Checks:
  - success through the hostname;
  - 403 without the token;
  - 403 after token revocation;
  - failure with the connector scaled to 0;
  - 404 for an unknown hostname on the tunnel;
  - `Cf-Ray` correlated in the logs.
- Stage 2, only if the entitlement is confirmed: the same, with a Private Origins A record to a private IP.
- Cost estimate:
  - about 1 to 2 engineer-days for the IaC and connector;
  - about 1 day for the checks;
  - recurring cost of about 10m CPU and 32Mi per connector, per `cloudflared.yaml` requests;
  - Cloudflare cost: Tunnel and Access at the current plan; Private Origins `unknown (not observed)`.
- The POC is removed by reverting the OpenTofu PR.

**Follow-up issues the report lists, which the owner files:**

1. mctl-gitops: Tunnel-first private MCP POC as above. P1.
2. mctl-gitops: Cloudflare account entitlement check for Private Origins and Unified Routing. P2, owner and account team.
3. .github: add "tenant-private downstream via Cloudflare hostname" to `docs/plans/mcp-gateway.md` downstream classes. P2.
4. mctl-api: tenant connectivity registration operation, after the POC. P3.

## Alternatives

- **ADOPT Private Origins as the single plane.** Dropped as the provisional verdict for three reasons:
  - it needs an account-team entitlement and Cloudflare One with Unified Routing (unknown status, unpublished pricing);
  - for connector-capable tenants it duplicates the plain Tunnel already in use;
  - it does not cover a tenant that refuses any Cloudflare component.
- **Build an MCTL-owned overlay (WireGuard, Headscale or similar).** Dropped because MCTL would own:
  - peers inside tenant networks;
  - an IP plan;
  - key rotation;
  - a relay with an availability SLO;
  - a new inbound surface in the cluster.
  That is exactly what the issue wants to avoid, and it brings no policy benefit, since authority stays in mctl-api either way.
- **Write the spike as an epic with work items now.** Dropped. The spike convention (`edge-config-kv-instant`) keeps the decision as a `SpikeDefinition` until the owner records it, and an epic before the decision would encode an unapproved plan.

## Platform impact

- Migrations: none. Backward compatibility: no runtime change. The report, manifest and `AGENTS.md` line are additive.
- Resource impact: none from the spike. The POC it designs would add one small connector pod and a few Cloudflare objects, sized in the report.
- Risks and mitigations:
  - *Treating Cloudflare as a policy authority.* The report states that Access is admission only and keeps tool authority in MCTL.
  - *Unverified vendor facts.* Everything not observed is tagged `unknown (not observed)` and listed as an open question.
  - *Manifest validation failure.* Run `validate.py` and the roadmap tests before pushing.
  - *Duplicate issue binding.* `.github#292` is not bound to any spike or epic today (checked).
